<!-- smg-doc-sync:7ff6e0347b9c8ee014cb15d8971b528422abb158:pd-non-streaming-json-content-type -->

## Concern

Document the HTTP PD router's non-streaming response Content-Type behavior on the concepts page. Verified in model_gateway/src/routers/http/pd_router.rs: streamed responses set text/event-stream (line 1607); a non-streaming decode body without logprobs is relayed with the decode worker's response headers preserved (forward_decode_body lines 1411-1427); when logprobs are requested, SMG builds the body itself via process_non_streaming_response (called only when return_logprob is true, lines 1403-1410) and every path returns through non_stream_pd_json_response (lines 1613-1624, call sites 1648/1657/1667/1671), which sets Content-Type: application/json instead of axum's application/octet-stream default. This corrects the hypothesis: the JSON helper does NOT cover the plain no-logprob relay path (that path preserves the decode worker's own headers, and the !return_logprob branch at line 1644 is unreachable from the helper's sole caller); it covers the logprob-merged response and its merge-failure fallbacks. One bullet is added to the existing "Failures, Cancellation, and Streaming" section of src/lib/content/concepts/routing/pd-disaggregation.md (verified undocumented there and in getting-started); no other pages changed.

## Evidence

Verified in pd_router.rs: non-streaming PD responses set Content-Type: application/json via non_stream_pd_json_response (lines 1613-1624) only on the logprob path — process_non_streaming_response's sole call site (line 1404) is guarded by context.return_logprob, and all its reachable returns (1648, 1657, 1667, 1671) use the helper. The no-logprob relay (1411-1427) preserves the decode worker's headers (Content-Type not filtered by should_forward_header_no_alloc, header_utils.rs:156-169), and streaming sets text/event-stream (line 1607). The PR correctly narrows the original hypothesis's overstatement that the plain relay path also gets application/json. The single added bullet on concepts/routing/pd-disaggregation.md is accurate, edits an existing page, makes no release claims, and the behavior is undocumented on both PD pages (no docs mention of the response Content-Type or octet-stream).

Source change: https://github.com/smg-project/smg/commit/7ff6e0347b9c8ee014cb15d8971b528422abb158

Verified against source `f5c25393c9111a90f02207896979a07e27f1baf1` and docs `f6d5ce025f8c241c2c384e9026114ea1c987d0e7`.

## Validation

- Scope/accuracy review: Verified in pd_router.rs: non-streaming PD responses set Content-Type: application/json via non_stream_pd_json_response (lines 1613-1624) only on the logprob path — process_non_streaming_response's sole call site (line 1404) is guarded by context.return_logprob, and all its reachable returns (1648, 1657, 1667, 1671) use the helper. The no-logprob relay (1411-1427) preserves the decode worker's headers (Content-Type not filtered by should_forward_header_no_alloc, header_utils.rs:156-169), and streaming sets text/event-stream (line 1607). The PR correctly narrows the original hypothesis's overstatement that the plain relay path also gets application/json. The single added bullet on concepts/routing/pd-disaggregation.md is accurate, edits an existing page, makes no release claims, and the behavior is undocumented on both PD pages (no docs mention of the response Content-Type or octet-stream).

The commit changes how `reasoning_effort` toggles thinking for chat templates that declare their own on/off words (Hy4-style: `high`/`no_think`): on such templates only the template's own off word turns thinking off, and the protocol-level `none`/`minimal` values no longer disarm the reasoning parser — any non-off value follows the template default. Current docs state unconditionally that `none`/`minimal` turn thinking off for templates with their own effort levels, which now contradicts source on main (commit f5c25393). One behavior, one concern spanning the two pages that describe the thinking decision.

concerns.title: docs: templates with their own reasoning_effort off words ignore the protocol none/minimal thinking switch
concerns.concern: On gRPC workers, for chat templates that toggle thinking through their own `reasoning_effort` on/off words (Hy4-style templates using `high`/`no_think`), thinking is turned off only by the template's own off word (`no_think`); the protocol values `none` and `minimal` no longer turn thinking off — any value other than the off word resolves to the template default (on, for default-on templates) and short-circuits the `thinking.type` toggle and the generic effort fallback. Renderers without their own off words (DeepSeek V4/V4.1, Kimi-K3) are unchanged: `none`/`minimal` still turn thinking off there. This fix is present on main via commit f5c25393c9111a90f02207896979a07e27f1baf1; release inclusion is unverified, so the docs should describe it as current main behavior.
concerns.evidence: Source commit f5c25393c9111a90f02207896979a07e27f1baf1; current model_gateway/src/routers/grpc/utils/parsers.rs lines 200-223 (`native_effort_thinking`: when `off_values` is non-empty, an off word returns Some(false) and every other value returns Some(on-word match || DefaultOn), bypassing `thinking_from_reasoning_effort`); crates/tokenizer/src/chat_template.rs `REASONING_EFFORT_ON_VALUES = ["high"]` / `REASONING_EFFORT_OFF_VALUES = ["no_think"]` and `ThinkingKeyName::ReasoningEffort`; commit test asserts `resolve_user_thinking(None, Some("none"), None, &tok) == Some(true)` for a Hy4-style mock.
